name: BMN 333
summary:
BMN 333 is BioMarin's weekly long-acting form of vosoritide for achondroplasia: BioMarin's own ICCBH 2026 poster calls it 'a long-acting version of vosoritide' and measures the vosoritide it releases. Its registration-enabling Phase 2/3 ASPEN (NCT07441876, 160 children, primary completion 2029-06) tests it head to head against Voxzogo (daily vosoritide), BioMarin's own product ($926.9mm in FY2025).
BioMarin says BMN 333 has the 'potential to become the new standard of care in achondroplasia' (8-K 0001048477-26-000015) and describes its efficacy by comparison with Voxzogo's (8-K 0001193125-26-010508). The gain from weekly dosing is already taken: Ascendis's weekly Yuviwel (navepegritide) was approved on 2026-02-27.
Held, and not priced: most BMN 333 revenue would be Voxzogo's patients switched between two BioMarin products. The potential 2030 launch falls before Voxzogo's US molecule patent expires on 2035-06-11. See refuse and flags_for_the_book.

therapy_mode.source: Voxzogo US label (book labels table, DailyMed setid 228e8560-04a4-4bb1-a81f-29531a9e4d27): 'to increase linear growth in pediatric patients with achondroplasia with open epiphyses'. BMN 333 dosing: BioMarin 8-K 0001048477-26-000015 (2026-08-06), Phase 1 'sustained exposure supporting weekly dosing'
therapy_mode.note: A weekly injection taken until the growth plates close, over years. That is chronic in the book's terms, the same as the Voxzogo daily regimen it would replace

forecast_start_year.source: NCT07441876 primary completion 2029-06, estimated (context file; book trials table, last update 2026-08-21; the Amass connector's quota is exhausted). Company-stated 'potential for a 2030 launch if results are positive' in search-result summaries of fiercepharma.com/pharma/biomarin-shows-promising-data-longer-acting-version-voxzogo and itiger.com/news/2557315803 ('Advances BMN 333 Toward 2030'). These pages were not opened because WebFetch is blocked, so a second reader should confirm the wording. A Phase 2 data update is due in 2027 (8-K 0001048477-26-000006)
forecast_start_year.note: Judgement. A launch in 2030 makes 2031 the first full year. The Phase 3 rule of two calendar years after primary completion (2029 + 2) gives the same year. Case for earlier: the design is seamless Phase 2/3, so there is no separate Phase 3 start to wait for. Case for later: a head-to-head superiority claim against an active comparator carries more readout risk than a placebo-controlled trial. Recorded only because it sets the cannibalisation window in refuse

economics_share.source: BioMarin is lead sponsor of NCT07441876 (book trials table). BioMarin FY2025 10-K 0001048477-26-000004 lists BMN 333 among its own clinical programmes with no partner. The 10-K text in the book (mdna, patents and risk_factors sections) has no royalty tied to vosoritide, Voxzogo, CNP or BMN 333
economics_share.note: Judgement: wholly owned. A royalty-free status rests on no royalty being found, not on a filing that states one. BioMarin's 10-K lists Prolynx, which also has long-acting CNP technology, as a competitor, not a licensor

refuse: HOLD: most revenue would come from the owner's own marketed product, Voxzogo (vosoritide). (1) BMN 333 releases the same active moiety. BioMarin's ICCBH 2026 poster P158 is titled 'Development of BMN 333, a long-acting version of vosoritide' and reports half-lives for 'released vosoritide from BMN 333' (medical.biomarin.com/en-us/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/06/ICCBH-2026_BMN_333_Development_poster_P158_MED-SC-0712.pdf). It is not a distinct CNP analogue. (2) The registration trial is head to head against Voxzogo (NCT07441876, 'BMN 333 Versus Vosoritide in Children With Achondroplasia'). It is built to win Voxzogo's prescribers, patients (children with open epiphyses) and label. (3) BioMarin positions it as the replacement: 'potential to become the new standard of care in achondroplasia' (8-K 0001048477-26-000002, 2026-02-23; 8-K 0001048477-26-000015, 2026-08-06), with 'expectations for BMN 333's efficacy compared to VOXZOGO's' (8-K 0001193125-26-010508, 2026-01-12). It presents 'Skeletal Conditions, namely VOXZOGO and BMN 333' as one revenue opportunity. (4) The installed base is large. Voxzogo has treated more than 5,000 children in more than 50 countries (BioMarin ACMG 2026 release, biomarin.com). Its net revenue was $926.9mm in FY2025 (10-K 0001048477-26-000004) and $472.4mm in H1 2026 (10-Q 0001048477-26-000016). (5) The route to market expansion is already taken. Weekly dosing is not new to the class: Ascendis's weekly Yuviwel (navepegritide) won FDA accelerated approval on 2026-02-27 for ages 2 and over, with 7 years of orphan exclusivity (Ascendis release, investors.ascendispharma.com). BMN 333's differentiating claim, higher free-CNP exposure, competes for already-treated patients rather than adding new ones. (6) Timing. A potential 2030 launch falls before Voxzogo's US molecule patent 8,198,242 (PTE to 2035-06-11) and its EU SPCs (to 2035-05-20) expire (10-K 0001048477-26-000004 patents section; book exclusivities). About five years of switched patients are therefore revenue BioMarin already books. Case against the hold: an untreated pool exists (achondroplasia is about 1 in 25,000 live births worldwide, and about 25% of people with it have open growth plates, per BioMarin's 2026 Voxzogo releases and voxzogo.com as summarised by search, not opened), and higher efficacy could draw some families who have declined treatment. BMN 333 also recaptures patients who would otherwise go to Yuviwel or oral infigratinib, and after 2035 it defends the franchise against generic daily vosoritide. BioMarin has not quantified any incremental patients, so the share of new against switched revenue cannot be sourced. Path to unhold: value BMN 333 at franchise level, as the nucresiran seed treats Amvuttra, once BMRN company rows carry a Voxzogo forecast. Fade Voxzogo from 2031, and count as BMN 333 revenue only the patients added beyond Voxzogo's base plus the post-2035 defence against generic vosoritide.
flags_for_the_book: Context file sort_evidence calls BMN 333 'a long-acting CNP analogue distinct from vosoritide'. BioMarin's own ICCBH 2026 poster (P158) calls it 'a long-acting version of vosoritide' that releases vosoritide, the same active moiety as Voxzogo. The context wording should be corrected.

No achondroplasia pool: lookup.py pool Achondroplasia returns nothing and epidemiology.csv has no row. lookup.py demand Voxzogo returns no CMS rows, which fits a paediatric drug with almost no Medicare beneficiaries, so the house Part D/B price convention has no anchor here. A later seed needs a published list price (WAC) instead.

The book holds Voxzogo's actual sales (asset_revenue, asset_id 95) but no forecast seed and no asset_revenue_regions split. If BMN 333 is ever unheld, BMRN company rows must fade Voxzogo against it, or the same achondroplasia patients are valued twice.

Duplicate or stray BMRN assets from trial interventions: 'BMN 111' (asset 1865) and 'Active BMN 111: Subcutaneous injection ...' (asset 1862) are both vosoritide (Voxzogo, asset 95) and should be folded into it by asset_merge.
